Filtering & Decimation Specification ### 7.1 Time Window Filtering (`--start`, `--end`) The CLI and export pipeline support flexible temporal windowing: - **Command-line flags**: - `--start `: Begins export at specified time. - `--end `: Terminates export at specified time. - **Allowed Formats**: 1. **Floating-point seconds from start**: e.g., `--start 30.5 --end 120.0` (sclices $30.5\text{ s} \le t_{\text{elapsed}} \le 120.0\text{ s}$). 2. **ISO 8601 UTC timestamp**: e.g., `--start 2026-10-27T14:33:00Z`. 3. **Standard colon time**: e.g., `--start 01:30 --end 05:45` ($MM:SS$). - **Boundary Validation**: - Requires $t_{\text{start}} < t_{\text{end}}$. - If $t_{\text{start}} \ge \text{Duration}$, export yields an empty sequence and emits a warning. - If $t_{\text{end}} > \text{Duration}$, clamping to EOF occurs without error. - Slicing semantics: Half-open interval $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}})$ or inclusive $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$. ### 7.2 Frequency & Stride Decimation (`--rate`, `--step`) High-frequency blackbox streams (.DAT: 50–200 Hz) and mobile logs (.txt: 10 Hz) often generate too much data for lightweight web viewers or spreadsheet editors. - **`--rate `**: Sets maximum output frequency in Hertz (Hz): - `--rate 1`: Exactly 1 record per second ($1.0\text{ Hz}$). - `--rate 5`: 5 records per second ($5.0\text{ Hz}$). - `--rate 0.5`: 1 record every 2 seconds ($0.5\text{ Hz}$). - **`--step `**: Stride decimation exporting every $N$-th record ($N \ge 1$). #### Uniform Time-Binning Algorithm: Given target sample rate $R\text{ Hz}$ with bin duration $\Delta t = \frac{1.0}{R}\text{ seconds}$: 1. Divide the time axis into intervals $I_k = [k \Delta t, (k+1) \Delta t)$. 2. For each interval $I_k$, select the record whose timestamp $t_i$ minimizes the absolute error $|t_i - (k + 0.5)\Delta t|$. 3. Guarantees uniform time spacing without time drift. ### 7.3 Critical Landmark Pinning & Event Preservation Decimation must NEVER eliminate mission-critical single-frame events. The decimator marks the following records as **pinned** so they survive decimation: 1. **Takeoff Event**: First record where `OSD.isMotorUp == 1` and `OSD.flyTime > 0`. 2. **Home Point Calibration**: The record where `HOME.isHomeRecord == true` is first registered or updated. 3. **Flight Mode Transitions**: Records where `OSD.flightMode` changes state (e.g. `P-GPS` $\to$ `Sport` or `Manual` $\to$ `Auto-RTH`). 4. **Safety Alerts & Warnings**: Any record with a non-empty `APP.warning` or `ShowSeriousWarning`. 5. **RTH Failsafe Activations**: Record where `GoHomeStatus` transitions to active. 6. **Max Altitude / Max Speed Extremum**: Points where maximum altitude or speed is achieved. 7. **Touchdown / Landing Event**: Final record where motors disarm (`OSD.isMotorUp == 0`). ### 7.4 Downsampling Algorithms (RDP & LTTB) - **Ramer-Douglas-Peucker (RDP) 3D**: Used for spatial vector reduction in KML and GeoJSON. Recursively finds the point of maximum perpendicular distance from the line segment connecting endpoints; if distance exceeds tolerance $\epsilon$ ($0.45\text{ m}$), the point is preserved. - **Largest Triangle Three Buckets (LTTB)**: Used for numeric time-series downsampling (altitude profiles, battery cell curves, velocity charts) in web dashboards. Downsamples 100,000 points down to 1,000–2,000 points while preserving peaks, valleys, and visual waveform fidelity. --- ## 8.
